chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Jameel ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'How many of the women were permissible for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever he so desired,' gesturing with his hand like this, 'and it is permissible for him,' meaning by the grasping of his hand.
ai.seo_question: How many wives were permissible for Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the doctrine of *Khasasiyyah* (special privilege), distinguishing the Prophet’s unlimited marital capacity from the general limit of four wives imposed on the rest of the Muslim community. The Imam’s gesture of grasping signifies that all wives he acquired remained exclusively lawful for him, a unique concession that underscores his spiritual and legislative authority. This distinction is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the specific exemptions granted to the Prophet during his lifetime.
